_comment: Story 12.12: the one exhibition Match between two language models.
This is NOT a tournament roster. It is a single, deliberately unranked
Deployment-versus-Deployment Match whose only purpose is that the flagship replay a
visitor lands on is two actual models fighting with their real reasoning attached,
instead of the two Baseline Bots that stood in for them for eight epics. Read
`configs/tournament.config.json` for the roster the leaderboard is computed from;
nothing here feeds that.
`ranked: false` on both sides. Be clear about what that does and does not buy:
it feeds `validateTournamentConfig`'s shared-quota warning and NOTHING ELSE. It is
never written into a Command Log, so the leaderboard's corpus reader cannot see it,
and it is not what keeps this Match off the board. What does is that the log is
schemaVersion 2.0.0 and `packages/cli/src/leaderboard.ts` validates candidates with
the v1 reader -- incidental protection, pinned by a test in
`apps/web/src/testing/exhibition-artefact.test.ts` that says so and names what to do
if a v2-capable reader ever lands. Read that block before making `loadCorpus` v2.
`seedCount` is 1 and is required by `parseRunConfig` rather than read by the
generator: this config describes one Match at `seedBase`, and the generator calls
`planMatch(seedBase, ...)` once. It is not a range to widen -- a second exhibition
Match is a second story, not a bigger number here.
Both models are Groq's `openai/gpt-oss-*` open-weight rows, and the choice is
measured rather than preferred. The acceptance criterion asks for per-decision
`reasoning`, and `reasoning` in a Command Log is `message.reasoning` from the
provider's response -- a field `openai-wire.ts` maps and does not invent. Probed
against the live endpoint on 2026-08-11 with the exact body the adapter sends:
`openai/gpt-oss-120b` returned 565 characters of reasoning and 128
`reasoning_tokens`; `openai/gpt-oss-20b` returned 1,115 and 261;
`llama-3.3-70b-versatile` and `qwen/qwen3.6-27b` returned no `reasoning` field at
all (qwen puts its deliberation in `<think>` tags inside `content`, which is the
raw response, not reasoning). A Match between the two llama rows would have
produced a log whose every `reasoning` was `null` -- the exact defect this story
exists to fix -- while passing every other check.
Both rows are on the free-tier allowlist in
`packages/providers/src/free-tier.config.json` (1,000 RPD, 8,000 TPM each), so
INV-8 holds unchanged and `assertFreeTierEndpoint` is not loosened. 8,000 TPM is
the binding constraint at roughly 1,000 tokens a call, which is why the generator
paces its own transport -- see `apps/web/scripts/build-exhibition-replay.mts`.
The two ids are not the model names: the frozen Agent id pattern is
`^[a-z0-9._:-]{1,96}$` and `openai/gpt-oss-120b` carries a slash. The `model`
field below is what actually goes on the wire.
`apiKeyEnv` names an environment variable. There is no field here that could hold
a key, and `config.ts` rejects a literal one by name shape.
